svg.title: The two ends of a region compared: all-gather plus GEMM against GEMM plus reduce-scatter
svg.desc: Two panels side by side, each with a locator strip marking which collective in the layer is shown, a serial timeline and an overlapped timeline. On the left, the all-gather end: the GEMM starts immediately on the token range the GPU already holds, so all three incoming transfers hide behind compute and the boundary falls from eight units to four. On the right, the reduce-scatter end: nothing can be sent until the first range has been computed, and the final range's reduction has no compute left beside it, so the boundary falls only from eight units to five.
svg.text: The two ends of a region do not overlap equally. Same collectives, same bytes, same arithmetic; what differs is whether compute has work to do before the communication starts.
at the start of a region
T0 is already local, so compute begins at once and
every transfer finishes behind it. Fully hidden.
at the end of a region
No head start, and a tail.
Nothing can be sent until T0 is computed, and T3's
reduction has no compute left beside it.
T0 to T3 are the four token ranges, one chunk each at t = 4. Bar lengths are illustrative.
